newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Island approves capital hike, rights offer.
newsitem.headline: Island approves capital hike, rights offer.

text.p: The board of Island Mining and Industrial Corp has approved an increase in its authorised capital to 500 million pesos from 50 million and a rights issue, the Philippine Stock Exchange said on Wednesday.

In an advisory to brokers, the exchange said the firm would convert into a holding company. It added that Island's board had approved at a meeting on Monday an increase in its authorised capital to 500 million pesos instead of 350 million pesos as proposed earlier.
The board also approved a two-for-one rights offer, or 100 million shares from the increased capital stock, to present shareholders, the exchange said.
The firm, which seeking to chang its name to IMIC Holdings Corp, also plans to raise the par value of its shares to one peso from one centavo per share.

Several Philippine mining firms have converted to holding firms, and diversified to more profitable ventures such as property development and financial services, in the past few months due to a downtrend in the mining sector.
